findings.title: refresh_token is set to the literal string "refresh_token" when missing
findings.body: When `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` is falsy, the code sets it to the literal string `"refresh_token"`. This is clearly a placeholder/debug value that was accidentally left in. This will corrupt the stored credential by overwriting a missing refresh token with a meaningless string, causing all subsequent token refresh attempts to fail permanently for that credential.

findings.title: Invalid Zod schema definition using z.string().toString() as object key
findings.body: `z.string().toString()` evaluates to the literal string `"ZodString"` at runtime, not a catchall key. The schema `minimumTokenResponseSchema` will have a property literally named `"ZodString"` that expects a number, rather than acting as a catchall for arbitrary numeric properties. This means the schema will not validate token responses correctly when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true, likely causing valid responses to fail validation or invalid ones to pass.

findings.title: prisma is used but never imported
findings.body: The `getClient` method calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` on line 96, but `prisma` is never imported in this file. The imports include `getAppKeysFromSlug`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, `HttpError`, `logger`, etc., but not `prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`. This will cause a `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` at runtime whenever a Salesforce credential is refreshed.

findings.title: Return type inconsistency causes runtime errors in callers expecting parsed tokens
findings.body: When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` object. When disabled, it returns whatever the `refreshFunction` returns (which varies: Axios responses for Zoho, HubspotToken objects for HubSpot, GaxiosResponse for Google). Callers like HubSpot (`hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn`), Zoho Bigin (`tokenInfo.data.error`), and Google Calendar (`res?.data`) access properties that don't exist on a raw `Response` object, causing `undefined` access and silent data corruption or crashes when syncing is enabled.

findings.title: Webhook endpoint does not restrict HTTP method
findings.body: The handler does not check `req.method`, so it accepts GET, DELETE, PUT, PATCH, etc. in addition to POST. A webhook endpoint that creates/updates credentials should only accept POST requests. Accepting other methods increases the attack surface and could lead to unexpected behavior with caching proxies or preflight requests.

findings.title: Race condition between findFirst and create/update
findings.body: The code first searches for an existing credential with `findFirst`, then either updates or creates it. Between these two operations, a concurrent request could create the same credential, leading to duplicate credentials for the same user+app combination. Since `userId` and `appId` are not unique constraints in the schema (as evidenced by the `findFirst` usage), this can result in multiple credentials for the same user-app pair, with unpredictable behavior on which one gets used.

findings.title: credentialId passed as userId to refreshOAuthTokens
findings.body: The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is `credentialId` (the credential's database ID), but the function expects `userId` (the user's ID). When credential syncing is enabled, the sync endpoint will receive the credential ID instead of the user ID in the `calcomUserId` parameter, causing it to look up tokens for the wrong entity.

findings.title: Uncaught exception when decryption or JSON parsing fails
findings.body: If `symmetricDecrypt` throws (e.g., wrong key, corrupted data) or `JSON.parse` throws (decrypted content is not valid JSON), the error is unhandled and will result in an unformatted 500 response. Since this is an externally-facing webhook endpoint, malformed payloads are expected and should be handled gracefully with a 400 response.

findings.title: tokenResponse.success check is dead code after parseRefreshTokenResponse change
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` now throws an error if parsing fails (line 21-23 of that file), so it never returns a result with `success: false`. The expression `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data` on line 264 will always evaluate to `tokenResponse.data`. While not a crash, the spread `...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)` is misleading and the `tokenResponse.success` check gives a false sense of safety. If `parseRefreshTokenResponse` behavior changes in the future, this pattern silently produces `false` being spread (which is a no-op) instead of handling the error.

findings.title: No authentication on outbound request to credential sync endpoint
findings.body: The `fetch` call to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends the user's `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` without any authentication header, API key, or webhook secret. If the endpoint URL is compromised or misconfigured, any party that can observe or intercept the request could enumerate user IDs and app slugs. The inbound webhook requires a secret, but the outbound sync request does not verify the identity of the sync endpoint.
